task: independent source review of proposed cookie procedures

verdict_A.reason: All seven listed controls, four admin cases, exact synthetic set/read/delete values, invalid-input checks, collision stop, cleanup and safe evidence boundaries are represented. The inventory permission-denied and reload dimensions remain explicitly unverified; these proposals are executable manual handler procedures but do not alone close every inventory dimension.

verdict_B.reason: The schemas, UI direct-run path, optional permission, manifest, wrapper delegation and expected result shapes match source. No live-site cookie or account secret is used. The proposal correctly avoids claiming admin, permission or confirmation enforcement from Tools Run. One source-anchor range for confirmation is inaccurate; no behavioral expectation depends on it.

findings.finding: The inventory case dimension includes permissions, and the stabilization plan calls for relevant permission-denied recovery. The proposed steps only require permission present and correctly refuse to treat direct Tools Run as a dispatcher denial. Keep permission denial unverified until a separate dispatcher-path procedure and receipt are authored and run; do not close this dimension from these cases.

The reload instruction is conditional on an allowed verified artifact and explicitly leaves reload unverified when none exists. This is safe and honest, but it cannot itself produce a completed reload cell; a later runtime lane must supply the artifact, exact receipt and observed reload evidence.

The anchor cites dispatch.ts 850-920 for privileged confirmation, but that span covers execution and result delivery. Cite the gate and confirmation code around the earlier effective-tier and confirmation path for this claim.

The preflight necessarily reads the returned cookie object in the inline Tools result if a same-name collision exists, despite the fixture instruction saying not to read a pre-existing cookie. Clarify that the operator must stop without inspecting or copying its value; the exact-name filter still prevents a broad cookie read.
